correctness.rationale: Exact Pareto integration gives the oracle H representation and covariance. The Hilbert Lindeberg condition holds since the largest summand H norm is bounded by sqrt(gamma/n), and covariance operators converge with integrable trace. Critical Poisson convergence follows by Pareto extremal point-process convergence and a <=2 epsilon small-jump H second-moment bound. Supercritical collapse follows from tightness of sample mean minus log n and an H-norm vanishing clipped-tail remainder. MLE substitution is controlled by direct log-Lipschitz bounds, with a faster normalization in the subcritical case. A Poisson fourth-cumulant calculation yields the exact variance increment. The embedded checker passed 68 formula and numerical assertions; finite checks are not treated as proofs.

value.rationale: The tuning parameter in an existing Pareto goodness-of-fit test changes null calibration across three natural sample-size regimes. A new compensated-Poisson quadratic limit and exact positive linear critical variance excess identify a nontrivial failure of simply extending the fixed-weight Gaussian limit. The supercritical typical-value collapse has an explicit rate for every deterministic gamma/n->infinity. This is a motivated statistical boundary, not a routine sample-size tweak, and no unproved claims about rejection power are inferred.
